To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified four protein peaks that are statistically significant for classifying lung cancer from mass spectra of serum samples, and that these proteins are consistent with the literature on biomarkers in lung cancer.

(1) the preprocessing steps we have used in our experiments are important for biomarker discovery and that (2) a linear support vector classification method, with the training and test samples used to select the features for classifying the mass spectra, is a promising approach to disease classification from mass spectra.

(a) the mass spectral data obtained from serum samples are suitable for disease classification; (b) the mass spectra are not affected by the choice of the protein matrix used in the mass spectrometry experiments; and (c) the mass spectra can be used for classification with a small number of peaks, and with various discrimination methods.
